notes: Demo files are stored in Git LFS (see .gitattributes). Clone with `git lfs install` first, or the .dem files arrive as ~130-byte pointer stubs.

Per D5, every entry records how its era was established. Date demos from seasonal asset names in their string tables, never from protocol numbers - protocol 3 / network 24 spans at least 2015 through 2026 and dates nothing.
Reproduce any field below with `python tools/inspect_demo.py walk|date <file>`.

demos.eraEvidence: String-table assets: sum20_fire_fighter_style1 and @20_handsome_devil (Summer 2020), rglgg_medal, etf2l_2018_bronze, hwn2019_bat_hat, Competitive Mode voice lines. Supersedes an earlier '~2015' estimate that was inferred from the protocol pair and was wrong.
demos.serverIdentityCaveat: serverName is the hostname cvar - operator-chosen free text, often an advert. The bytes support 'the server called itself FACEIT', not established provenance.
demos.knownIssues: Fails to play in the current live TF2 client (client-side SendTable schema validation, same class of failure as the July 2023 break). The file itself is intact.
demos.notes: First corpus entry. See docs/FORMAT_NOTES.md and docs/SPEC.md.

demos.eraEvidence: ETF2L listing timestamp plus the .dem's own mtime inside the archive.
demos.whyItMatters: The only POV demo in the corpus, and the only source of dem_usercmd (120,624) and dem_consolecmd (9,782) commands - z1800.dem contains zero of either, so those payload paths were completely untested before this file. Also has 5 dem_signon rather than 3.

demos.eraEvidence: ETF2L listing timestamp plus the .dem's own mtime inside the archive.
demos.whyItMatters: Second SourceTV demo, from an unrelated server (serveme.tf) and a different map. Together with the POV file it established that the one-byte-short dem_stop terminator is universal TF2 behaviour rather than damage to z1800.dem.

corpusGaps.preTwentyTwenty: EMPTY, and not for lack of trying. Checked 2026-08-07: RGL launched 2019 so its oldest demos are the same era as these. ETF2L's listing goes back to Sept 2014 but the files have rotted - every demo id below ~12010 returns HTTP 404, and the live floor is id 12025, dated 2020-07-23. ESEA's SourceTV demos shipped with expiry dates and were never permanently downloadable, so there is nothing to recover; community Mega collections catalogued on teamfortress.tv in 2013 are long dead. sizzlingstats, which did keep demos, is gone.
corpusGaps.consequence: The parser has no historical coverage and no test that would reveal its absence. See D5 - the schema-driven design has to be right by construction, because it cannot be verified.
